title: Home guide: the balloon-in-a-bottle lung model
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Muscles and bones (7C); the particle model (7G)
source: Written for science/y7 lesson 18 (Home practical guide and safety card: balloon-in-a-bottle lung model (portal worksheet; an adult cuts the bottle))
intro: Read it all first, then do it with an adult nearby.

practical.aim: Model how the diaphragm changes the volume and pressure in the chest.
equipment: A plastic bottle (an adult cuts off the bottom)
safety: An adult cuts the bottle; cut edges can be sharp: tape over them
An adult knows what you are doing and stays nearby
Clear a space; tidy up and wash your hands afterwards
method: Push one balloon into the neck of the bottle and stretch its opening over the neck: this is the lung.
Cut the neck off the second balloon and stretch it over the open bottom of the bottle; hold it with the elastic band: this is the diaphragm.
Pull the bottom balloon down gently. Watch the balloon inside.
Push it up. What happens now?
Label: bottle = chest, inside balloon = lung, stretched balloon = diaphragm.
practical.adult: Adult step: cutting the bottle and taping its edge.

questions.q: Give one strength and one weakness of the model.
questions.a: Strength: it shows that pulling the diaphragm down increases the volume and draws air in. Weakness: the ribs and intercostal muscles do not move; real lungs are not one balloon.
